anatomy.intro: Rounded leaf bumps develop on a powdery blue-green rosette as it matures.

parts.function: The raised rounded bump is part of the leaf, not a water droplet or insect.
parts.label: Caruncle

parts.function: A dusty wax layer gives the leaf its pale matte finish.
parts.label: Farina

parts.function: The broad leaf stores water and supports photosynthesis.
parts.label: Fleshy blade

parts.function: The smallest new leaves may not yet show the cultivar's bumps.
parts.label: Young center

flowers.text: Echeverias raise clusters of tubular, bell-like flowers above their foliage. NC State notes that the genus attracts bumblebees and hummingbirds. Mountain Crest Gardens lists pink blooms for 'Raindrops'.

growth.note: The smallest leaves can be smooth before their bumps develop; compare successive mature leaves to follow that change.

stages.text: A small rosette may initially have few or no bumps.
stages.title: Grow young leaves

stages.text: Maturing leaves show the rounded structures characteristic of the cultivar.
stages.title: Develop raindrops

stages.text: The rosette expands; offsets may be infrequent.
stages.title: Broaden the crown

habitat.text: 'Raindrops' is a cultivated Echeveria. The genus ranges from the southwestern United States into South America; its thick rosette leaves store water through dry periods. This selection combines broad blue-green leaves, a waxy surface and raised rounded bumps that become more conspicuous as the leaves mature.

Echeveria Raindrops: compact low blue-green rosette of broad rounded succulent leaves, dusty matte wax, pink edges. Mature outer and middle leaves each carry a single smooth rounded droplet-like mound (caruncle) on the upper surface near its outer end; smallest center leaves have no bumps. Markers: 1 a clearly visible rounded caruncle, 2 matte waxy leaf surface, 3 broad fleshy leaf blade, 4 young central leaves. No flowers or offsets. The caruncles are part of leaf tissue, not transparent water droplets.

lookalikes.name: Echeveria pulidonis
lookalikes.text: Pulidonis has smooth pointed leaves with fine red margins. Mature 'Raindrops' has broader rounded blades carrying conspicuous bumps, though small new leaves can be smooth.

mature.text: The nursery describes a rosette reaching about 6 inches across and producing few offsets. Give the expanding outer leaves room to spread without rubbing neighboring pots.

nameStory.text: The nursery credits hybridizer Dick Wright. The name describes its droplet-like leaf bumps; they are normal cultivar growth and should not be scraped off.
